agent.finish_summary: Fixed a regression in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py: the `_handle_closing_keyword` method's handling of the `END IF` keyword had an incorrectly negated condition (`if not (self._block_stack and self._block_stack[-1] == 'IF'):`), unlike the correct, non-negated logic used for END FOR/END WHILE/END LOOP/END CASE. This caused statement splitting to misbehave for SQL containing IF...END IF blocks inside BEGIN...END (e.g. PL/pgSQL function bodies and LOOP/IF/END IF/END LOOP sequences), which corresponds to the reported 'issue194 splitting function' and 'parse endifloop' failures. Changed the condition to `if self._block_stack and self._block_stack[-1] == 'IF':` to match the pattern of the other closing-keyword branches. Verified via ad-hoc tests (now removed from the workspace) that: CREATE FUNCTION bodies with DECLARE/BEGIN/IF/END IF/END parse as a single statement; BEGIN/LOOP/IF/END IF/END LOOP/END followed by a separate statement splits into two statements; plain multi-statement SQL still splits correctly; nested IF/END IF pairs inside BEGIN...END still work. No other files were changed.
